source.title: Some Fundamental Aspects about Lipschitz Continuity of Neural Networks

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper varies network width and label noise and reports test-loss outcomes bearing on generalization, using Lipschitz bounds as an additional measure.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports Lipschitz-bound trends, optimizer and regularizer effects on those bounds, and other measurements. These do not directly measure the claim versions' generalization outcomes, so they are not rows. Figure 10 reports test loss across label-shuffling levels, but the text does not state the held-out accuracy or chance-level comparison required by V1.
record.test_reason: The study directly measures held-out loss across widths, extending V2's question to CNNs, ViTs and additional datasets. Its Lipschitz measurements alone do not test the other versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate for the width experiment: the authors interpret double-descent-like Lipschitz trends as implicit regularization through overparameterization. Their broader conclusion also emphasizes substantial changes from initialization, fidelity of the lower Lipschitz bound and interactions among label noise, capacity and smoothness. They do not establish universally decreasing test loss with width.
record.recipe_differences: The study sweeps CNN width and reports test loss alongside Lipschitz bounds; it does not use the exact V2 architecture and dataset setup.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported width trend is tested across architectures and datasets; explicit Lipschitz constraints reduce the Double Descent trend in an additional experiment, but that experiment is outside the specified V2 setup.

fits_no_version.finding: Lipschitz bounds rise during training, exhibit width-dependent double descent and vary with label noise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Input-space Lipschitz estimates exhibit systematic training-, capacity- and noise-dependent trends; this is distinct from magnitude-aware parameter sharpness in V7.

fits_no_version.finding: Adam produces larger Lipschitz bounds and parameter displacement than SGD; dropout lowers Lipschitz estimates.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer and dropout choices affect function smoothness. These measurements alone do not establish the held-out-performance effects in V4 or V6.

record.problems: Generalization values in the relevant width-sweep figures are plotted without tabulated values. Results are averaged over 4 runs; the main text does not state test-loss values or uncertainty intervals for Figure 7.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 10 reports test loss for a CIFAR-10 label-shuffling sweep, but the text provides no stated held-out accuracy or chance-level comparison, so no V1 result row was retained. Other width-sweep test-loss figures are similar additional settings; the retained CIFAR-100 result is the main-text example.

untested.parts: Figure 10 reports test loss under label shuffling, without establishing the joint comparison of near-perfect random-label training accuracy, natural-label accuracy above chance and random-label held-out accuracy at chance.

Classification-error trends and the exact original MNIST/downsampled-CIFAR-10 recipe are not established by the retained rows. Parameter count near sample count is a theoretical threshold, not a reported measurement of zero training error.
No controlled convolutional-versus-fully-connected held-out-performance comparison or local-connectivity intervention.
The Adam-versus-SGD experiment measures Lipschitz bounds and parameter displacement, without reporting comparative held-out performance.
No batch-size sweep measuring held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets.
The dropout sweep reports Lipschitz bounds, without comparative test error.
No magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation sharpness measure, generalization-gap ranking or comparison against norm and margin measures.
No removal of examples selected by label memorization followed by retraining and comparison with random removal.

missing.what: The explicit largest-width test-loss upturn after the second descent. Although rows_left_out broadly declares additional width sweeps, describing them as similar omits this material exception; add a condition-specific outcome row.
missing.locator: Appendix S3.9, remark on Figure S12; setup in S2.6.2

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for any listed version. Other width-sweep settings and Figure 10 are already declared in rows_left_out. No numerical curve values can be recovered reliably from the supplied text, so verdicts use explicit qualitative statements.

versions.untested_parts: Does not report the specified held-out accuracy versus chance comparison, or the named Zhang et al. architectures and training setup.
Tests CNNs on CIFAR-100 and other settings, not the specified one-hidden-layer ReLU networks on MNIST and downsampled CIFAR-10.

rows.subject: CNN models (width sweep)
rows.operation_detail: Varied CNN width and measured test loss.
rows.uncertainty: Results averaged over 4 runs; figure shows no stated uncertainty value.
rows.note: The text says test loss mirrors the Lipschitz-bound trend: it rises up to the interpolation threshold and decreases beyond it. Values are not stated in text.
rows.check: Section 4 explicitly describes test loss decreasing beyond the interpolation threshold. The measure is cross-entropy loss, not classification error. Training stops at gradient norm 0.01 or 15,000 epochs after at least 500 epochs; zero training error is not explicitly established.
